nodes.name: Ni-SiC Composite Electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Nickel coatings containing well-dispersed, submicron (150-500 nm) SiC particles were electrodeposited from an agitated, modified Watts nickel electrolyte at 60 °C using a current density of 10-100 mA cm^{-2} from an electrolyte containing 10 g dm^{-3} SiC at a current density of 6 A dm^{-2}. Over 20 surfactants including anionic, cationic, and nonionic types were evaluated for their influence on the surface and tribological properties of the nanocomposite coatings. A surfactant concentration of 0-3 g dm^{-3} was used.

nodes.name: Ni-MoS2 High-shear Dispersion Electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The hydrophobic nature of MoS₂ presents a challenge to electrodeposition of composite coatings due to particle agglomerates present in an aqueous plating bath. Electrolyte preparation using high-shear mixing is shown to be an effective way to achieve a narrow particle size distribution and stable particle dispersions. The Ni-MoS₂ coating had a compact structure.
